chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is not befitting for the Imam that he should move/turn when he has offered the greeting (Salām) until those behind him have completed the prayer (Salāt).

He (the narrator) said: And I asked him about the man who leads the prayer, is it befitting for him to follow up with his companions after the greeting? So he said: He glorifies (God) and goes wherever he wishes for his need, and a man should not follow up specifically to follow up the Imam.

key_terms.إِلَى الْإِمَامِ: To the Imam / For the prayer leader

ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette for an Imam after saying the final greeting in prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the post-prayer etiquette, emphasizing that the Imam’s departure is contingent upon the congregation's completion rather than a rigid waiting period for specific follow-up rituals. It clarifies that the Imam is not bound to delay his exit to facilitate the followers' supplications, thereby balancing leadership decorum with practical flexibility. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of communal prayer dynamics, ensuring order without imposing unnecessary burdens on the leader.
